Amelia — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; attaching a short evidence bundle and a mapping CSV for your engineers. Happy to do a 30-45m workshop to walk these with your IdP/IT team.

1) Tenant segmentation
- Redwood Private supports both single-tenant (per-customer VPC) and multi-tenant logical segmentation within the same deployment. For our multi-tenant mode we provide strict namespace isolation: customer tenants are logically separated at the data-plane level and access controls are scoped by tenant id.
- Cross-tenant data access is not possible via the standard API surface: service-level routing enforces tenant ids on requests. Only platform operators with approved, audited emergency access (JIRA + approval workflow) can where absolutely necessary access multiple tenants; such actions are logged and require two-person review.

2) SCIM provisioning
- We support SCIM 2.0 with bulk / delta operations. Provisioning modes: full-sync (initial import), incremental PATCH-based syncs, and event-driven provisioning via webhook if you prefer.
- Deprovisioning enforcement: when a SCIM PATCH removes or deactivates a user, tokens issued to that user are marked for revocation. Active session revocation happens asynchronously but typically within 30–120 seconds depending on session length and caching (we surface a session invalidation endpoint for immediate effect).
- For enterprise scale (100k+ users) we recommend our incremental sync with SCIM state cursors — we provide guidance and a reference mapping file (attached).

3) RBAC & delegated admin
- Out-of-the-box roles: Org Admin (manage org-wide settings, billing), Tenant Admin (manage users, routes, model pinning within tenant), Support Admin (create incident tickets, limited diagnostic access), Read-only Auditor.
- Custom roles: yes — we support custom role creation with selectable permissions (create, update, manage tokens, view logs, impersonate limited). Role definitions are stored in the control plane and enforced in the runtime.
- Delegated admin workflows: you can assign a Tenant Admin limited to a subset of routes and models; we also support attribute-based access control (ABAC) for advanced policies (subject attributes + resource tags).

4) SSO (SAML / OIDC)
- Both SAML 2.0 and OIDC are supported for SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
- Group-to-role mapping: we provide mapping rules that can consume IdP group assertions (SAML) or claims (OIDC) and convert them to RBAC roles. Rules can be simple mappings or conditional expressions (e.g., if memberOf contains X and department=Y then role=TenantAdmin).
- Just-in-time (JIT) provisioning: supported for SAML/OIDC with controlled defaults. We recommend combining JIT with SCIM for long-term source-of-truth and clean deprovisioning.

5) Audit & session controls
- Audit log retention: default 90 days; enterprise retention tiers available up to 7 years as an add-on. All admin operations, role changes, and emergency accesses are logged with immutable entries and an append-only sequence for tamper evidence.
- Session revocation: session tokens support immediate revocation via the admin API; there is also automated token expiry and rolling key rotation.

Amelia — quick follow-up to address both asks and propose next steps.

- Emergency access: yes, the emergency access workflow is configurable. We support customer-managed approvers (you can bind approver roles to specific user lists or AD groups) and require two independent approvals by default. The emergency access event exports via the admin API in JSON or CSV; we can provide a sample export as part of the evidence bundle.
- Cross-tenant enumeration: confirmed — Tenant Admin roles are denied listing or enumerating tenant identifiers other than those explicitly scoped to them. Our default Tenant Admin scope is strictly tenant-aware. We will include test steps for your security validation checklist.
